items.readable_text:
Content:
When we divide a fraction by a whole number, say [MATH: {\color{red}{2}},] the idea is to

Content:
- split the fraction into [MATH: {\color{red}{2}}] equal parts, and
- determine the fraction that makes up each part.

Content:
For example, suppose we wish to find the value of

Content:
[MATH: \dfrac{4}{5} \div 2.]

Content:
Let's start by drawing the fraction model for [MATH: \dfrac45\mathbin{:}]

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/f345c5d4630be0995779cde0327f55b4]

Content:
We need to divide this fraction by [MATH: {\color{red}{2}}.] To do this, we draw a horizontal line through our fraction that splits it into [MATH: \color{red}2] equal parts.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/5381a543704612749e4f2b2712e1f7d7]

Content:
We only need to determine the fraction that makes up one of the parts. Therefore, we can focus on only one row (i.e., the bottom row).

Content:
Now, we remove all the shaded parts not in the bottom row.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/54a9e7ebe3c900b2bdcfe928092fb128]

Content:
From the picture on the right, we obtain that the shaded part represents [MATH: \dfrac{4}{10}] of the whole. Therefore, we conclude that
[MATH: \dfrac{4}{5} \div 2 = \dfrac{4}{10} \, .]

lesson.readable_text:
Item 1 — Tutorial: Introduction

Content:
When we divide a fraction by a whole number, say [MATH: {\color{red}{2}},] the idea is to

Content:
- split the fraction into [MATH: {\color{red}{2}}] equal parts, and
- determine the fraction that makes up each part.

Content:
For example, suppose we wish to find the value of

Content:
[MATH: \dfrac{4}{5} \div 2.]

Content:
Let's start by drawing the fraction model for [MATH: \dfrac45\mathbin{:}]

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/f345c5d4630be0995779cde0327f55b4]

Content:
We need to divide this fraction by [MATH: {\color{red}{2}}.] To do this, we draw a horizontal line through our fraction that splits it into [MATH: \color{red}2] equal parts.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/5381a543704612749e4f2b2712e1f7d7]

Content:
We only need to determine the fraction that makes up one of the parts. Therefore, we can focus on only one row (i.e., the bottom row).

Content:
Now, we remove all the shaded parts not in the bottom row.

Graphic:
[IMG: /graphics/54a9e7ebe3c900b2bdcfe928092fb128]

Content:
From the picture on the right, we obtain that the shaded part represents [MATH: \dfrac{4}{10}] of the whole. Therefore, we conclude that
[MATH: \dfrac{4}{5} \div 2 = \dfrac{4}{10} \, .]

---
